title: Perfecting the Tactile Paper Sheet UX: Spotlight Search, 3D DevBlog & Final Polish
summary_excerpt: Following up on yesterday's UX critique, elevated the portal experience—crafting the signature Tactile Paper Sheet design system, keyboard-driven spotlight search (Ctrl+K), and interactive 3D DevBlog Coverflow.
full_story:
Following up on yesterday's self-critique where the UX still felt incomplete, today's objective was relentless visual and interactive perfection.

I dedicated today to turning raw functional components into a unified, tactile experience. We established the Tactile Paper Sheet Design System, introducing warm ivory canvas tones (#FBF9F4), deep carbon ink contrast (#161616), physical paper border elevations, and official KLD Green accents across all student, employer, and administrative views.

Universal Spotlight Search & 3D Stage DevBlog

To make navigation effortless, I engineered the keyboard-driven universal Spotlight Search modal (Ctrl+K) that queries api/search-jobs.php with live debouncing. Furthermore, I built this interactive 3D Coverflow DevBlog on the About Us page so our entire daily journey is recorded transparently for our professor and peers.

Presentation Readiness

With both design variations prepared and our core workflows rigorously validated across mobile and desktop devices, we are fully prepared to present our dual-design project to our professor with utmost confidence.
key_takeaways: Perfected the Tactile Paper Sheet design tokens across all student, employer, and admin interfaces.
Engineered universal Spotlight Search (Ctrl+K) with live API debounce.
Constructed the interactive 3D perspective DevBlog Coverflow and modal reader.
Ensured both design variations are polished and presentation-ready for our professor.

title: Team Git Collaboration, Mentoring Groupmates & The Dual-Design Strategy
summary_excerpt: Balanced multi-subject coursework with core development, mentored groupmates on Git and GitHub collaborative workflows, and initiated a dual-design strategy to present two strong prototypes to our professor.
full_story:
When I woke up in the morning, well what do you expect—I quickly finished my required tasks for other subjects and immediately dove straight back into system development.

Today marked a major team milestone: I conducted a hands-on mentoring session for my groupmates to teach them how the system works, how our file hierarchy is organized, and how to use Git and GitHub for collaborative development. They learned remarkably fast and were eager to contribute.

Dual-Design Presentation Strategy

To maximize our impact during the midterm presentation, we planned a dual-design strategy: my groupmates would develop their design variation, while I developed mine. This ensures we can present 2 distinct, fully functioning design directions to our professor.

The 11:30 PM Build & UX Reflections

I completed that day's development build at 11:30 PM. However, stepping back to evaluate it, my design still felt incomplete and the UX did not fully satisfy my standards. I resolved then and there to start developing further tomorrow to bring the user experience to perfection.
key_takeaways: Taught groupmates Git version control and GitHub collaborative repository workflows.
Established the dual-design strategy to develop and present 2 unique prototype options.
Completed the 11:30 PM core build milestone covering applicant review and admin controls.
Critiqued UX shortcomings and established high-fidelity refinement goals for the next day.

title: The Start of the Madness: All-Day Coding Sprint & 1:00 AM Optimization Marathon
summary_excerpt: Pushed through an intensive full-day coding marathon from early morning to 1:00 AM—building the zero-DB JSON persistence engine, session state synchronization, password entropy meter, and end-to-end application workflows.
full_story:
August 27 was the true start of creating this madness. The moment I woke up in the morning, I jumped directly into the codebase to develop and optimize the core architecture even further.

For the entire day, I worked non-stop on our zero-database data architecture. I built includes/data-helper.php, establishing atomic file reads/writes for our JSON datasets and synchronizing live states into $_SESSION for zero database overhead and lightning-fast responses.

Security Algorithms & Shift Availability Matrix

I engineered the standalone client-side Shannon password entropy analyzer (password-strength.js) with real-time criteria checkmarks, role-based access control (RBAC), and built the interactive 18-slot weekly schedule availability time grid matrix for student job submissions.

Pushing Through to 1:00 AM

I coded and optimized straight through the evening and night, finally stopping at 1:00 AM on August 28, hoping that this intensive development foundation would be solid and comprehensive enough for our project.
key_takeaways: Engineered zero-database atomic JSON persistence and dynamic session synchronization.
Implemented real-time client-side password entropy scoring and visual strength feedback.
Built the 18-slot weekly schedule availability grid matrix for student applications.
Completed a grueling 16+ hour coding marathon ending at 1:00 AM for core engine stability.

title: Genesis of the System: Topic Selection, Architecture Drafting & Pure PHP Foundations
summary_excerpt: Kicked off on topic selection day—immediately drafted the architecture, cataloged requirements, explored UI inspirations, and began non-stop coding during every free hour adhering strictly to pure PHP with zero static HTML.
full_story:
Our journey began on August 26, 2026—the day our team picked the project topic for our COAL101 Web Systems and Technologies midterm lab project.

As soon as we chose the Campus Job Posting System, we didn't waste a single moment. We planned immediately, structured the project directory hierarchy, listed every functional module we would need, and researched modern design inspirations suited for a premier institutional portal.

Strict Stack Compliance: Native PHP, No Raw HTML

During our free time that day on campus, we started drafting the site. We strictly limited our stack to what our professor permitted: Native PHP, CSS, Bootstrap 5.3, and Vanilla JavaScript—with strictly no standalone HTML files as our professor instructed. Every page had to be dynamically composed via modular PHP components.

Lead Developer Dedication

As the lead of this development, I simply couldn't stop thinking about the system. I continued developing through another free period that same day and kept writing code up until we went home, determined to finish the foundational task.
key_takeaways: Selected the Campus Job Posting System topic and mapped all functional requirements.
Enforced pure Native PHP modular template architecture with zero static .html files.
Defined initial JSON datastore schemas for users, categories, jobs, and applications.
Developed continuously through campus free periods and after going home to build the skeleton.
